london.blurb: Museums, royal palaces, gardens and river views. Many of the big sights have timed entry, so booking ahead saves queueing.
london.tip1: Many major museums are free to enter, but special exhibitions are ticketed.
london.tip2: A single-day pass often beats buying each ticket separately if you plan three or more sights.

paris.blurb: Art, architecture and river cruises. The Louvre, Eiffel Tower and Versailles all work best with a pre-booked time slot.
paris.tip1: Book the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre ahead; same-day slots often run out.
paris.tip2: Versailles is a half-day trip from the centre, so plan it separately.

rome.blurb: Ancient sites, the Vatican and plenty of food stops. Combined tickets cover the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine Hill.

amsterdam.blurb: Canals, world-class museums and cycling. Popular museums and canal cruises are worth booking in advance.
amsterdam.tip1: The Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Anne Frank House use timed tickets.
amsterdam.tip2: Public transport passes can cover the city and the region.

madrid.blurb: The Prado, royal palaces and lively evenings. Madrid also makes a good base for day trips to Toledo and Segovia.
madrid.tip1: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen are close together on the Paseo del Prado.
madrid.tip2: Many day-trip tours leave from the city centre in the morning.

istanbul.blurb: Mosques, bazaars and Bosphorus cruises across two continents. Guided tours help with the old city's layered history.
istanbul.tip1: Dress modestly when visiting mosques; some close briefly for prayer times.
istanbul.tip2: A Bosphorus cruise is a relaxed way to see both shores.

lisbon.blurb: Hilltop viewpoints, historic trams and day trips to Sintra. Plan for hills and comfortable shoes.

lisbon.tip2: Tram 28 gets very crowded; go early or choose another route.

dubai.blurb: A global transit hub with long-haul routes in every direction.
dubai.tip1: Book popular attractions ahead in peak season.
dubai.tip2: Consider a desert safari or Burj Khalifa visit.

athens.blurb: Gateway to the Greek islands; summer schedules add many extra routes.
athens.tip1: Combine the Acropolis with the museum on the same day.
athens.tip2: Book island ferries in advance in summer.

esim.metaTitle: Travel eSIM | Mobile Data Abroad Without Roaming Fees
esim.metaDesc: How a travel eSIM works, who it suits, and what to check before you buy. Compare it with roaming and local SIM cards.
esim.title: Mobile data abroad, without roaming bills
esim.intro: A travel eSIM is a data plan you install on your phone before you fly. You land connected. No airport SIM queue, no surprise roaming charges.
esim.s1d: Your phone must support eSIM and be network-unlocked. Most phones from the last few years do.
esim.s2d: Choose your country or region and a data amount that fits your trip length.
esim.s3d: Scan the QR code on Wi-Fi before you leave, then turn on the plan when you land.
esim.h1: eSIM vs roaming vs local SIM
esim.p1: Roaming is the easiest but often the most expensive, and charges vary a lot by carrier and country. A local SIM is usually cheapest per gigabyte but means finding a shop, showing ID and swapping your physical SIM. A travel eSIM sits between the two: you set it up in advance and keep your own number active for calls and texts.
esim.p2: Confirm your phone is eSIM-compatible and unlocked, make sure the plan covers every country you will visit, and check how long the plan is valid after installation. Data-only plans don't include a phone number, so calls go through apps like WhatsApp.
esim.h3: How much data do you need?
esim.p3: Maps, messaging and email use little data. Video calls, streaming and hotspot sharing use much more. If you are unsure, pick a plan one size larger or one that can be topped up.
esim.q1: Will I keep my WhatsApp number?
esim.a1: Yes. Your normal SIM stays active in your phone; the eSIM only provides mobile data. WhatsApp and similar apps keep working with your usual number.
esim.a2: Install it on Wi-Fi before you leave, then switch the data plan on when you land. Many plans start counting from first use, but check the validity on the plan page.
esim.q3: Can I use my phone as a hotspot?
esim.a3: That depends on the plan. Some allow tethering and some don't, so check the details of the plan you choose.
esim.q4: What if my phone doesn't support eSIM?
esim.a4: Then an eSIM won't work. Check your phone settings or the manufacturer's site, or consider a local SIM or pocket Wi-Fi instead.

tr.metaTitle: Airport Transfers | Book a Pickup Before You Fly
tr.metaDesc: Pre-booked airport transfers: how they work, when they beat taxis and public transport, and what to check before you book.
tr.title: A driver waiting when you land
tr.intro: Book a private or shared transfer before you travel. You see the price up front and avoid haggling or queuing for a taxi after a long flight.
tr.s1d: Add the airport, your destination and the number of passengers and bags.
tr.s2d: Choose between standard cars, minivans and larger vehicles based on group size.
tr.s3d: Add your flight number so the driver can track delays, then meet them in arrivals.
tr.h1: When a transfer beats a taxi
tr.p1: Pre-booking is most useful when you arrive late at night, travel with children or lots of luggage, or land somewhere you don't know the local taxi rules. You know the price before you go, and the driver is expecting you.
tr.p2: Many big cities have fast, cheap train or metro links from the airport. For solo travellers with light bags and daytime arrivals, that is often the best value. Compare the door-to-door time and cost for your own trip.
tr.h3: What to check before you book
tr.p3: Look at the free-waiting time, how the driver finds you, what the cancellation terms are and whether child seats are available. Giving your flight number lets the driver adjust if you are delayed.
tr.q1: What if my flight is delayed?
tr.a1: If you give your flight number when booking, the provider can usually track your arrival. Check the waiting-time policy shown on the booking page.
tr.q2: Can I book a return transfer?
tr.a2: Most providers let you add a return journey when booking. Check the pickup time and place for the way back.
tr.a3: Many providers offer them on request. Add them when you book, as they can't always be arranged on the day.
tr.a4: You pay the provider when you book. TicketsJet doesn't take payments or add fees.

comp.metaTitle: Flight Delay & Cancellation Compensation | Check Your Claim
comp.metaDesc: Were you delayed or cancelled? Learn how EU flight compensation rules work and how to check whether you can claim.
comp.title: Delayed or cancelled flight? Check if you can claim
comp.intro: Under EU and UK rules, passengers can be owed up to €600 when a flight is cancelled or badly delayed. Check your flight in a couple of minutes.
comp.s1d: You need the flight number, date and the reason you were told for the delay or cancellation.
comp.s2d: The service tells you whether your flight is likely to qualify under the rules.
comp.s3d: If it qualifies, a claims company can handle the airline for you, usually for a share of any payout.
comp.p1: EU Regulation 261/2004 can apply to flights departing from an EU airport, or arriving in the EU on an EU airline. Fixed compensation of €250, €400 or €600 depends on the distance. Common qualifying cases are cancellations with short notice, arrivals three or more hours late, and denied boarding. The UK has a similar scheme.
comp.h2: When you are usually not entitled
comp.p2: No compensation is due for extraordinary circumstances outside the airline's control, such as severe weather or air traffic control strikes. You may still be entitled to meals, hotel and rebooking in those cases.
comp.h3: Claim yourself or use a service
comp.p3: You can claim directly from the airline for free, but it can take time and letters back and forth. Claims services handle the process in return for a fee that is normally taken only if the claim succeeds. Read the fee before you sign.
comp.q1: How long do I have to claim?
comp.a1: Time limits depend on the country where you claim and range from one to several years. Claim as soon as you can, while you still have your documents.
comp.a2: Your booking confirmation, boarding pass and any messages from the airline help. A claims service can often start with just the flight details.
comp.a3: Checking eligibility is normally free. If you use a claims service, the fee is taken from the compensation, so read the terms first.
comp.a4: No. We link to a third-party claims service. TicketsJet isn't a party to your claim and doesn't give legal advice.

cars.guideLead: New to renting abroad? Read our guide:
cars.a1: You collect the car with a full tank and return it full. It's usually the fairest fuel policy. You only pay pump prices for the fuel you actually use.
cars.q2: Do I need a credit card?
cars.a2: Many rental desks require a credit card in the main driver's name for the security deposit. Some offers are marked as not requiring one. Use the filter in the search above.
cars.a3: Basic rates usually include a damage waiver with a high excess. Compare what each offer includes, and consider full-insurance options if you want a lower excess.
cars.a4: Many offers include free cancellation. The exact conditions are shown on each offer before you book, so check them before you pay.
cars.a5: Booking is completed with the rental provider. TicketsJet is a search tool and never takes payment or adds fees.
cars.affiliateNote: We may earn a commission if you book through this partner, at no extra cost to you.
cars.trust2: Check deposit, insurance and cancellation before you book
cars.info1d: Most companies require the driver to be at least 21. Young driver surcharges may apply under 25. Maximum age limits vary by company.
cars.info2d: You need a valid driving licence held for at least one year. An International Driving Permit may be required depending on your licence and destination.
cars.info3d: A security deposit is usually blocked on a credit card in the main driver name. The amount varies by company and car group.
cars.info4d: Basic rates include a damage waiver with an excess. Compare what is included and consider full insurance to reduce the excess. Rules vary by company.
cars.info5d: Full-to-full is the fairest fuel policy. Check whether mileage is unlimited or capped. Conditions vary by offer.
cars.info6d: GPS, child seats and additional drivers are usually charged separately. Add them at booking if needed.
cars.q6: When is the cheapest time to rent a car?
cars.a6: Prices vary by destination and season. Booking in advance and comparing offers usually gives better rates.
cars.a7: Airport pickups are convenient but may carry a surcharge. City centre locations can be cheaper. Compare both options.
cars.q8: Can I rent without a credit card?
cars.a8: It depends on the company. Some require a credit card for the deposit; others accept debit cards or cash. Check the offer details.
cars.a9: The excess is the amount you pay towards a claim before insurance covers the rest. Full insurance options can reduce it to zero.

help.metaDesc: Answers to common questions about searching and booking flights and car rentals with TicketsJet.
help.booked: Booked already? Your reservation is held by the airline or provider you booked with. Contact them directly for changes, cancellations or refunds.
help.a1: We search airlines and travel agents to find the best flight options. We don't charge booking fees. You book directly with the provider.
help.q2: How can I find the cheapest flight using TicketsJet?
help.a2: Try searching 'Everywhere' to explore lowest-cost destinations, use the flexible-date calendar, and compare mid-week departures which are usually cheapest.
help.q3: Where should I book a flight to right now?
help.a3: Check the fare board on our homepage or run an 'Everywhere' search from your home airport to see the current budget deals across Europe, the US and Asia.
help.q4: Do I book my flight with TicketsJet?
help.a4: No. You book directly with the airline or travel agent on their platform. TicketsJet acts strictly as a search engine showing you the aggregated choices.
help.a5: Flights and car rentals are our focus. For hotels, our Stays search opens Booking.com in a new tab, where you compare and book. TicketsJet doesn't compare hotel prices yet.
help.a6: TicketsJet compares leading car rental companies to bring you competitive prices, free-cancellation options and clear fuel policies.
help.q7: What happens after I've booked my flight?
help.a7: You will receive a confirmation email directly from the vendor or airline you purchased from. Reach out to them directly for any support questions. They hold your reservation.
help.q8: Can I book a flexible flight ticket?
help.a8: Yes. Many airlines provide tickets that allow date changes without fees. Look for the flexible filter during your search.
help.a9: Never. Our service is free for travellers. We earn a commission from providers when you book through our links. At no extra cost to you.
help.q10: Is my payment handled by TicketsJet?
help.a10: No. All payments are made directly on the provider's secure platform. We never see or store your payment details.

about.metaDesc: TicketsJet is an independent travel search engine comparing flights and car rentals across many providers.
about.h1: A search engine that works for travellers
about.p1: TicketsJet is an independent travel search engine. We compare flights across many airlines and travel agents, and car rentals across leading rental companies, with more travel tools on the way.
about.h2: What we do. And what we don't
about.p2: We show you the market, side by side, and send you directly to the provider to book at their exact price. We never add booking fees, never mark up prices and never handle your payment. Your reservation always lives with the airline or rental company you book with.
about.p3: When you book through links on TicketsJet, the provider may pay us a commission. This costs you nothing extra and never affects the prices you see. Read our affiliate disclosure for the full picture.

priv.metaDesc: How TicketsJet collects, uses and protects your data.
priv.p1: TicketsJet ("we") operates ticketsjet.com, a travel comparison search engine. We do not process bookings or payments. Those happen directly with the providers you book with.
priv.l1: Search data. Routes, dates and destinations you search, used to display results.
priv.l2: Usage data. Anonymous analytics such as pages visited and device type, used to improve the site.
priv.l3: Cookies. Used for site functionality, analytics and advertising (including Google AdSense) and affiliate tracking by our travel partners.
priv.p2: We never see or store your payment details, passport information or booking records. These are handled entirely by the airline, hotel or rental provider you book with.
priv.p3: Our search tools and outbound links are provided together with travel partners who may set cookies to attribute bookings. Advertising on this site may be served by Google AdSense, which uses cookies to show relevant ads. You can manage ad personalisation in your Google settings and cookies in your browser settings.
priv.p4: Under the GDPR and similar regulations, you may request access to or deletion of any personal data we hold. Contact us via the details on this website and we will respond within 30 days.
priv.unsplash: We display destination photos served by Unsplash (images.unsplash.com); loading them shares your IP address with Unsplash.

terms.metaDesc: The terms governing your use of the TicketsJet comparison service.
terms.p1: TicketsJet is a comparison search engine for flights, accommodation and car rentals. We aggregate offers from third-party providers. We are not a travel agent, airline, hotel or rental company, and we are not a party to any booking you make.
terms.p2: All bookings are made directly with third-party providers, on their platforms and under their terms. Prices, availability, changes, cancellations and refunds are governed by the provider's own conditions. Always review the final price and terms on the provider's site before paying.
terms.p3: Prices and availability are sourced live from providers and can change between search and booking. We work to keep information accurate but cannot guarantee it, and we are not liable for discrepancies confirmed at the provider's checkout.
terms.p4: You may use TicketsJet for personal, non-commercial travel planning. Scraping, automated querying or reselling of our service is not permitted.
terms.p5: To the fullest extent permitted by law, TicketsJet is not liable for any loss arising from bookings made with third-party providers, including cancellations, schedule changes or service quality.
terms.p6: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the site after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.

aff.metaDesc: How TicketsJet earns commissions through affiliate partnerships, and what that means for you.
aff.p1: TicketsJet is a free comparison service. To keep it free, we participate in affiliate programs with airlines, online travel agencies, hotel booking platforms and car rental companies.
aff.p2: When you click a link on TicketsJet and complete a booking on a provider's site, that provider may pay us a commission. This commission comes out of the provider's marketing budget, it is never added to your price. You pay exactly what you would pay going to the provider directly.
aff.p3: Commissions do not influence the order or content of search results, which are driven by price and relevance. Our guides and recommendations reflect what we genuinely believe helps travellers, regardless of commercial relationships.
aff.p4: Outbound links to booking providers on this site should be assumed to be affiliate links. They are additionally marked with sponsored link attributes for transparency.
